study.title: Like Mount Zion, unshakable
study.intro: Psalm 125 is a song of security. Pilgrims arriving at Jerusalem could see the mountains rising all around the city, and the psalm turns that view into a promise: as the hills surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds His people. Those who trust Him are as steady as Mount Zion. The psalm also prays that evil will not rule forever and that God will do good to the upright.
study.context: Jerusalem sits on a ridge ringed by higher hills, including the Mount of Olives to the east. This Song of Ascents may come from a time when foreign rulers held power over the land, which explains the concern that 'the scepter of the wicked' not remain. It ends with the same blessing as Psalm 128: 'Peace be upon Israel.'
study.peopleNote: No author is named. The psalm speaks of those who trust the LORD, the righteous and upright, contrasted with those who turn to crooked ways. God is never portrayed as a human figure in planned art.

verses.title: Steady as a mountain
verses.heading: Those who trust are like Mount Zion
verses.meaning: 'Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion. It cannot be moved; it abides forever.' Mountains are the most solid things people know. Storms come and go, but the mountain stays. Trusting God gives a person that kind of stability. This does not mean you never feel shaken inside, but it means the ground beneath your life is secure, because it rests on the God who never changes.
verses.context: Mount Zion was the hill in Jerusalem where David brought the ark and where the temple stood. Psalm 46:5 says God is within her and she will not be moved. Jesus compared those who hear and obey Him to a house built on rock (Matthew 7:24-25).
explore: Mount Zion
The hill of Jerusalem where the temple stood, often a name for the city and God's dwelling.
Abides
Remains and continues firmly over time without being removed or changed.
verses.reflect: What would change if you saw yourself as secure as a mountain because you trust God?
verses.alt: A great rocky hill rising solidly above a valley under clear sky.

verses.title: Surrounded by the LORD
verses.heading: As the mountains surround Jerusalem
verses.meaning: 'As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds His people, both now and forevermore.' Pilgrims could see it with their own eyes: Jerusalem cradled by hills on every side. God does the same for His people. He is not only ahead of you or behind you; He is all around you. And this protection is not temporary. It lasts now and forever, through every season of life.
verses.context: Jerusalem is surrounded by higher ground, including the Mount of Olives to the east. 2 Kings 6:17 tells of Elisha's servant seeing hills full of horses and chariots of fire around them. Zechariah 2:5 promises God will be a wall of fire around Jerusalem.
explore: Surround
To encircle completely on every side, leaving no side unprotected.
Forevermore
From this moment on and without end; God's protection does not expire.
verses.reflect: Picture God surrounding you on every side. Which side of your life most needs that reminder today?
verses.alt: A walled city nestled among rolling hills at golden hour.

verses.title: Evil will not rule forever
verses.heading: The scepter of the wicked will not rest
verses.meaning: 'For the scepter of the wicked will not rest upon the land allotted to the righteous, so that the righteous will not put forth their hands to injustice.' Wicked rulers may hold power for a time, but God will not let them rule His people's inheritance forever. Why? Because long oppression can wear down even good people until they start to compromise. God limits evil's reign to protect the hearts of the faithful.
verses.context: A scepter was a ruler's staff, a symbol of authority. Israel at times lived under foreign rulers. 1 Corinthians 10:13 says God will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, and Psalm 37:9-10 promises evildoers will be cut off.
explore: Scepter
A staff held by a king as a sign of ruling power and authority.
Allotted
Given as a share or portion; Israel's land was divided by lot among the tribes.
verses.reflect: How does it encourage you that God puts limits on how long evil can press on His people?
verses.alt: An ornate staff lying abandoned in the dust beside a field boundary stone.

verses.title: Do good to the good
verses.heading: To the upright in heart
verses.meaning: 'Do good, O LORD, to those who are good, and to the upright in heart.' The pilgrim prays a simple prayer: bless those who live rightly. 'Upright in heart' means more than outward good behavior; it means a heart that is straight with God, honest and sincere. God loves to do good to people like this, and we are invited to ask Him to bless those who walk faithfully.
verses.context: Psalm 73:1 says God is good to Israel, to those pure in heart. Matthew 5:8 says the pure in heart are blessed, for they will see God. 1 Samuel 16:7 reminds us that the LORD looks at the heart.
explore: Upright
Straight, honest and morally right; not crooked in thought or conduct.
Heart
In Scripture, the center of a person's thinking, choosing and feeling.
verses.reflect: Whom can you pray for today, asking God to do good to them?
verses.alt: A farmer at dawn opening a gate for a neighbor's flock.

verses.title: Crooked paths and peace
verses.heading: Peace be upon Israel
verses.meaning: 'But those who turn to crooked ways the LORD will banish with the evildoers. Peace be upon Israel.' The psalm warns that people who wander off onto twisted paths will share the fate of evildoers. This is not about people who stumble and repent but those who choose crookedness. Then it closes with a blessing: peace on God's people. The choice is between a crooked road that leads away and a straight road that leads to peace.
verses.context: Proverbs 2:15 describes those whose paths are crooked and devious. Isaiah 59:8 says the way of peace they do not know. Galatians 6:16 echoes the blessing: 'Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.'
explore: Crooked ways
Twisted paths, a picture of choosing deceit and wrongdoing instead of God's straight path.
Banish
To drive away or remove; here God sending evildoers away from His people.
verses.reflect: Is there a crooked path you are being tempted to take? What would choosing the straight road look like?
verses.alt: A straight road and a winding side trail splitting apart in rolling country.
